# Pattern Review: Brackenford Hall

## Input Quality and Limitations

The log covers two events in one month. E1 and E2 are two distinct instances, but neither has a diagnosis or investigation record. Both causes are unknown.

## Summary

| Candidate | Occurrences | Distinct Instances | Cause Consistency | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reported projector cut-outs: E1, E2 | 2 | 2 | Unknown; no diagnoses supplied | High that the reported symptom recurs; low that it reflects one shared cause |

## Genuine Patterns

The wording “The projector cuts out” recurs across E1 and E2. This establishes a repeated reported symptom, not a genuine shared-cause pattern. With causes unknown in both entries, diagnosis work is needed before judging the underlying pattern.

## Misleading Surface Patterns

E1 and E2 use identical wording, but that does not establish identical causes. Different causes are also not demonstrated. Treating these reports as one diagnosed fault could misdirect a fix.

## Isolated Signals, Not Yet Patterns

There are no diagnosed isolated causes to report. E1 and E2 remain separate, undiagnosed instances within the repeated symptom group.

## Suggested Actions for Human Approval

Investigate each instance separately and record the evidence establishing its cause. A person should then compare the diagnoses, assess whether any recurring driver matters, and approve any proposed fix or process change.

## What This Sample Cannot Tell You

This complete two-event log cannot establish a shared cause, a longer-term trend, or an appropriate fix. The absence of investigation records also means it cannot show whether either issue was resolved.
